newsitem.title: USA: Pay-to-play rule keeps Hough off Pinellas Cty deal.
newsitem.headline: Pay-to-play rule keeps Hough off Pinellas Cty deal.

text.p: William R. Hough & Co voluntarily withdrew as senior manager for a Pinellas County, Fla., housing bond issue after discovering an employee had donated $480 to a county commissioner's election campaign, a hosuing authority official said Tuesday.
Hough officials were not immediately available for comment.
The $50 million mortgage revenue bond deal was priced last week with George K. Baum & Co as senior manager, said Darlene Kalada, director of the Pinellas County Housing Finance Authority.
"It didn't affect the pricing on the deal at all. We were made aware of the potential problem early," Kalada said.
According to Kalada and the Jacksonville Times-Union, Hough withdrew from the deal to avoid violating Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board rule G-37.
The rule bars municipal bond firms from doing business with an issuer for two years if firm members make campaign donations exceeding $250 to issuer officials.
"Our firm, unfortunately, had to resign (from the deal) to comply with MSRB," the newspaper quoted Hough senior vice president Helen Feinberg as saying.
"It was a voluntary thing," Kalada told Reuters. "They discovered it, they reported it. Of course we all expected an exemption because it was self-discovered."
She said Hough had asked the National Association of Securities Dealers for a waiver of the two-year rule but that the request was denied and was under appeal.
NASD officials said they could not immediately comment.
Hough is headquartered in St. Petersburg, Fla., which is the county seat for Pinellas.
